title: Mean-field collapse theorem — mouse-at-median is a corollary, not a biological null
premise_under_test: On a structureless (Erdos-Renyi) graph under the rank-2 all-ones-broadcast operator (P18 PASS), the network quiescent fraction QF reduces at mean-field order to a function of ONLY the two operator coordinates (total_pa, snare_factor), with per-neuron deviations O(1/sqrt(K)) in mean in-degree K. Therefore any two profiles with matched coordinates produce near-identical QF, so the conserved profile cannot be statistically special against a coordinate-matched random null beyond finite-N fluctuations -> its percentile sits near the median. This DERIVES the P8 corrected-control result (mouse 38% ~ median) from first principles; the worm/fly deviations from median (P8: 28%/26%, significant) are the residual that lives on the REAL connectomes and is absent from the mouse random graph.
analytic_claim: mu_i = K * W_syn * snare_factor * <w> * r + I_baseline + total_pa (homogeneous mean field). Self-consistent r* = Phi(mu(r*), sigma_eff); QF = fraction below threshold = a function of (total_pa, snare_factor). Cell-to-cell input fluctuation CV^2 = Var_i(mu_i)/<mu_i>^2 = Theta(1/K) because the weighted in-degree s_i is a sum of ~K i.i.d.-ish terms (E[s]=K*mu_w, Var[s]~K*E[w^2]).

G_P3_1_fluctuation_scaling.rule: On the mouse ER substrate (build_mouse_random_graph), the per-neuron weighted-in-degree CV^2 = Var_i(s_i)/mean_i(s_i)^2 scales as 1/K with mean degree K. Fit log10(CV^2) vs log10(K) across K in {10,20,40,80,160} (>=3 graph seeds each); the slope must lie in [-1.3, -0.7].
G_P3_1_fluctuation_scaling.on_fail: the mean-field fluctuation law does not hold on this substrate; the mouse-at-median corollary loses its mechanism; re-open the analytic reduction.

G_P3_2_mouse_median_collapse.rule: The corrected dual-coordinate (P8 Match#2b) mouse percentile must sit in the median band [25%, 75%], consistent with QF collapsing to the two coordinates (class identity adds nothing beyond magnitude on the structureless graph). Source: artifacts/v7_match2b/v7_match2b_verdict.json.
G_P3_2_mouse_median_collapse.too_special: mouse_percentile <= 10% would CONTRADICT the theorem (class identity special despite a structureless graph) -> escalate / re-open P1/P18.
G_P3_2_mouse_median_collapse.note: worm/fly percentiles (P8: 28%/26%, significant) are EXPECTED to deviate below median — that residual is the real-connectome structure signal (motivates P16), not a contradiction of the mouse corollary.

confirmatory_non_load_bearing.G_P3_3_degree_sweep: Optional overnight: re-run the mouse QF-percentile pipeline at mean_degree in {20,40,80,160}; the conserved percentile should converge toward 50% as ~1/sqrt(K). VOID if baseline rate drifts >0.5 Hz (operating-point not preserved). Not required for the load-bearing verdict; deferred.

claim_impact: PASS demotes v7_final_summary §8.1 ('conserved target list NOT statistically special in mouse') from an embarrassing empirical null to a DERIVED mean-field corollary that PREDICTS the ~median percentile a priori. Combined with P8, the whole Sub-Q1 percentile pattern is reframed: mean-field predicts compression toward median for all three; the worm/fly significant deviations are the connectome residual, mouse (random graph) has none.
anti_target_engineering: Slope band [-1.3,-0.7] and median band [25,75] fixed from the analytic 1/K and 1/sqrt(K) laws BEFORE measurement. A slope far from -1, or a mouse percentile <=10%, are accepted contradictions that re-open upstream blocks.
